candidates.structural_interaction: Wood directing Earth cross-polarity — reach shaping stability into structured cultivation
candidates.k2_overview: Your Earth moves as the Steward: ground that keeps. This is stewardship in its home element, doubled: holdings maintained, households provisioned, value settled into soil. What enters your care appreciates. The risk is weight for its own sake. Keep the estate serving the family, not the family serving the estate.
candidates.k2_functional: You maintain relentlessly: the fixed fence, the paid tax, the kept schedule.

k2_domain_readings.Wealth: Your wealth is literal ground: property, durables, enterprises with deeds. In your element, holdings hold. Diversify just enough that one bad season cannot take the whole farm.
k2_domain_readings.Savings: You save geologically: layers on layers, bedrock reserves. The craft is knowing enough. Set the number, then let the surplus fund life above ground.
k2_domain_readings.Steady love: You love in permanence: home built, name shared, decades assumed. It is the marrying ground itself. Bring the assumption out loud sometimes. Even bedrock likes being chosen again.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, firm ground is scarce. You hold each piece of it close, and what you own wears well.

angles.drive: Making a thing last is a craft you practice without noticing. Waste feels to you like a small loss of control, so you repair what you own rather than replace it. Under your hands, old things keep earning their place.
angles.cost_self: Making things last keeps you in control of what you own. You put hours into repairs instead of the better thing on offer, because replacing feels like waste. Your weekends go to mending things worth less than the time they take.
angles.cost_others: You keep old things going for everyone around you. Fixing beats choosing for you, and those who share your things live with your repairs rather than their own picks. They seldom get to pick something new for themselves.

angles.drive: Saving comes first for you, before the treat and the trip. A cushion is what lets you relax, and you put money away rather than enjoy it. A bad month never finds you short.
angles.cost_self: Saving first is the quiet skill under everything you own. You would rather be covered than pleased, and the good thing you can afford keeps waiting. Year after year, the treats you promised yourself stay on the list.
angles.cost_others: You save for the people you love before spending on them. A safe future is the gift you trust, and you give them the cushion rather than the dinner. Whatever comes, your family has something to fall back on.

angles.drive: Being loyal costs you less than leaving ever would. The known thing keeps you safe, and you hold what is already yours instead of looking elsewhere. The people you stand by know exactly where to find you.
angles.cost_self: Your loyalty stays put, and it pays in people who stay. You keep choosing what is yours rather than ask if it chooses you too. Under it all, you want proof that the bond runs both ways.
angles.cost_others: Loyalty is how you love, and you show it by staying. You stand by the people you chose rather than look around, and you let the staying speak for you. Those you love rarely hear it in words.

friction.define: As a friction, what you own weighs more each year. You keep it near for comfort, and your hands stay full with no space for anything new.

angles.drive: Letting a thing go is harder for you than keeping it. Having it within reach makes you feel safe, so you keep things for a someday need rather than a present use. What no longer matters to you is yours to part with.
angles.cost_self: Keeping everything is your insurance against going without, and it costs you. You would rather pay to store a thing than risk needing it, and your money guards what you never use. You rent space for things that give nothing back.
angles.cost_others: You hold onto things you cannot bring yourself to drop. You keep a thing rather than take its space back, and the house fills from the walls in. You leave the people you live with less space in their own home.

angles.drive: Staying put feels like safety, whatever the place becomes. Moving asks more of you than staying, so you keep the known rather than go toward the better. You are free to move and take your safety with you.
angles.cost_self: Being hard to move keeps your life steady and small. You would rather weigh a move than make one, and the better place is taken while you weigh it. You lose the chance to go in the time you spend deciding.
angles.cost_others: You stay, and hold the people closest to you in place. Staying matters to you more than moving somewhere better together, and you set the whole house to your speed. You make them wait on a move you are not making.

angles.drive: You hate to spend, even on the things you can plainly afford. Spending feels like losing control, and you hold onto the money rather than buy what you wanted. You get to enjoy money that is already yours.
angles.cost_self: Hating to spend means you rarely overpay and rarely enjoy. You would rather keep the money than spend it, since spending feels like a loss already begun. Left with the money, you go without the thing it was for.
angles.cost_others: Spending on the people you love comes no easier than spending on yourself. Giving less feels safer than giving more, and you cut back on them first. You take what you save out of their share.

edge.lead: Earth runs through your wealth, your family and your career. It is the money put by that makes a bad month ordinary, the old chair you fix instead of buying a new one, and the job you see through to a proper finish.
